parameters.query:
SELECT title, url, source
FROM discoveries
ORDER BY id DESC
LIMIT 8;

parameters.jsCode:
const articles = $input.all().map(item => item.json); // 🔥 include linkLabel in grouped input const grouped = articles.map((a, i) => `${i + 1}. ${a.title} URL: ${a.url} SOURCE: ${a.source} LINK_LABEL: ${a.linkLabel || "Read More"}` ).join('\n\n'); const prompt = ` You are a senior frontend editor writing a high-quality weekly newsletter. Using the articles below: ${grouped} Write a concise, insight-driven newsletter. STRICT RULES: - Generate ONLY inner content blocks. - Do NOT include , , or outer wrapper tables. - Use clean semantic HTML only. - Return ONLY valid HTML. --- 🔥 LINKING RULES (VERY IMPORTANT): - ALWAYS use the provided LINK_LABEL exactly - NEVER write "Read Full Breakdown" - NEVER create your own anchor text - DO NOT embed links inside sentences - Links must be placed as separate elements after paragraphs Example:

Insightful explanation...

View GitHub Repo Each article must use its LINK_LABEL. --- 🔥 WRITING STYLE: - Do NOT describe trends passively - Make strong statements - Explain WHY it matters - Highlight trade-offs or risks Bad: "developers are exploring..." Good: "developers are shifting toward..." Bad: "this suggests..." Good: "this indicates a clear shift toward..." --- Use this exact structure:

Frontend Weekly

Performance & Tooling

...

LINK_LABEL

AI & Developer Experience

...

LINK_LABEL

Architecture & Patterns

...

LINK_LABEL

Recommended Reads

  • LINK_LABEL — short explanation
--- Additional rules: - Professional tone for senior frontend engineers - Avoid fluff - Avoid generic greetings - 350–450 words - End with a short CTA paragraph linking to https://elegantfrontend.training Return ONLY valid HTML. `; return [{ json: { prompt } }];
